title: AutoSettings automations
description: An AutoSettings automations.yaml file: automations (when/if/then rules) and profiles (named sets of actions).

automations.description: Rules: when a trigger fires and all conditions are true, run the actions.

profiles.description: Named sets of actions that can be applied and reverted as a unit.

id.description: Unique, stable id, e.g. gaming-mode. Generated from the name when missing.

name.description: Friendly name shown in the app and the activity log.

enabled.description: Set to false to keep the automation without running it.

cooldown.description: Minimum time between two runs, e.g. 30s. Triggers during the cooldown are ignored.

triggers.description: Any of these starts the automation.

conditions.description: All of these must be true for the actions to run.

priority.description: When active profiles change the same setting, the higher priority wins.

type.description: The trigger type.

then.title: Computer started
then.description: Fires once each time the computer starts, before anyone signs in.

type.description: Fires once each time the computer starts, before anyone signs in.

include_fast_startup.description: Also fire when Windows starts with Fast Startup (the default shutdown mode on most PCs, which is really a hibernate). Turn off to react to full restarts only.

then.title: User signed in
then.description: Fires when a user signs in to Windows. The user who signed in is available to conditions and to actions as {{ user }}.

type.description: Fires when a user signs in to Windows. The user who signed in is available to conditions and to actions as {{ user }}.

user.description: Only fire when one of these users signs in. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

session.description: Which kind of sign-in: at the computer (local), over Remote Desktop (remote), or either (any).

then.title: User signed out
then.description: Fires when a user signs out.

type.description: Fires when a user signs out.

user.description: Only fire when one of these users signs out. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

then.title: Screen locked
then.description: Fires when a user locks the computer (Win+L, or automatically after inactivity).

type.description: Fires when a user locks the computer (Win+L, or automatically after inactivity).

user.description: Only fire when one of these users locks the screen. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

then.title: Screen unlocked
then.description: Fires when a user unlocks the computer.

type.description: Fires when a user unlocks the computer.

user.description: Only fire when one of these users unlocks the screen. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

then.title: App started
then.description: Fires when an app starts.

type.description: Fires when an app starts.

app.description: The app(s) that start. Use the exe name (chrome or chrome.exe), a full path (C:\Games\game.exe) or wildcards (*steam*). Use * for any app.

instance.description: Many apps (browsers, games, Steam) start several processes. 'first' fires only when the first copy starts; 'any' fires for every process.

user.description: Only fire when one of these users start the app. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

then.title: App closed
then.description: Fires when an app exits.

type.description: Fires when an app exits.

app.description: The app(s) that close. Use the exe name (chrome or chrome.exe), a full path (C:\Games\game.exe) or wildcards (*steam*). Use * for any app.

instance.description: 'last' fires only when the last running copy exits (the app is fully closed); 'any' fires for every process that exits.

user.description: Only fire when one of these users close the app. Accepts a user name (samet), DOMAIN\name, a SID, or wildcards (admin*). Leave empty for any user.

then.title: App focused
then.description: Fires when a window of the app becomes the active (foreground) window.

type.description: Fires when a window of the app becomes the active (foreground) window.

app.description: The app(s) that gain focus. Use the exe name (chrome or chrome.exe), a full path (C:\Games\game.exe) or wildcards (*steam*). Use * for any app.

title.description: Only fire when the window title matches one of these patterns (wildcards allowed, e.g. *YouTube*).

then.title: App no longer focused
then.description: Fires when the app stops being the active window, because another app was focused or the app was closed or minimized.

type.description: Fires when the app stops being the active window, because another app was focused or the app was closed or minimized.

app.description: The app(s) that lose focus. Use the exe name (chrome or chrome.exe), a full path (C:\Games\game.exe) or wildcards (*steam*). Use * for any app.

title.description: Only fire when the title of the window that lost focus matches one of these patterns.

type.description: The condition type.

then.title: All of
then.description: True when every nested condition is true. (The top-level condition list already works like this; use `and` inside `or`/`not`.)

type.description: True when every nested condition is true. (The top-level condition list already works like this; use `and` inside `or`/`not`.)

conditions.description: The conditions that must all be true.

then.title: Any of
then.description: True when at least one nested condition is true.

type.description: True when at least one nested condition is true.

conditions.description: At least one of these must be true.

then.title: None of
then.description: True when none of the nested conditions is true.

type.description: True when none of the nested conditions is true.

conditions.description: None of these may be true.

then.title: User is
then.description: True when the user involved is one of the listed users. In machine automations this is the user from the event (who signed in or started the app); in personal automations it is you.

type.description: True when the user involved is one of the listed users. In machine automations this is the user from the event (who signed in or started the app); in personal automations it is you.

users.description: User names, DOMAIN\name, SIDs or wildcards.

then.title: Time of day / weekday
then.description: True during a time window and/or on certain weekdays. Windows that cross midnight (after 22:00, before 06:00) are supported.

type.description: True during a time window and/or on certain weekdays. Windows that cross midnight (after 22:00, before 06:00) are supported.

then.title: Power source
then.description: True when the computer runs on the given power source.

type.description: True when the computer runs on the given power source.

then.title: Battery level
then.description: True when the battery charge is within the given range.

type.description: True when the battery charge is within the given range.

above.description: True when the charge is above this percentage.

below.description: True when the charge is below this percentage.

then.title: App is running
then.description: True when one of the apps is running (or, with running: false, when none is).

type.description: True when one of the apps is running (or, with running: false, when none is).

app.description: App patterns (exe name, path or wildcards).

running.description: Set to false to require that none of the apps is running.

then.title: App is focused
then.description: True when one of the apps currently has the active window.

type.description: True when one of the apps currently has the active window.

then.title: Full-screen app active
then.description: True when a full-screen app, game or presentation is in the foreground.

type.description: True when a full-screen app, game or presentation is in the foreground.

active.description: Set to false to require that no full-screen app is active.

then.title: Wi-Fi network
then.description: True when connected to one of the Wi-Fi networks (or, with connected: false, when connected to none of them).

type.description: True when connected to one of the Wi-Fi networks (or, with connected: false, when connected to none of them).

connected.description: Set to false to require that you are not on any of these networks.

then.title: Number of monitors
then.description: True when the number of connected monitors is within the range. Handy for docked/undocked laptops.

type.description: True when the number of connected monitors is within the range. Handy for docked/undocked laptops.

then.title: Profile is active
then.description: True when the profile is currently applied (or, with active: false, when it is not).

type.description: True when the profile is currently applied (or, with active: false, when it is not).

active.description: Set to false to require that the profile is not applied.

type.description: The action type.

then.title: Apply profile
then.description: Applies a profile. The settings it changes are remembered and restored when the profile is reverted, automatically or with profile.revert.

type.description: Applies a profile. The settings it changes are remembered and restored when the profile is reverted, automatically or with profile.revert.

profile.description: Id of the profile to apply.

revert_on.description: When to undo the profile automatically. 'auto' pairs it with the trigger: app_focused → app_unfocused, app_started → app_closed, logon → logoff, unlock → lock; other triggers never revert automatically.

continue_on_error.description: Keep running the next actions even if this one fails.

then.title: Revert profile
then.description: Undoes an active profile, restoring the settings it changed. Does nothing if the profile is not active.

type.description: Undoes an active profile, restoring the settings it changed. Does nothing if the profile is not active.

profile.description: Id of the profile to revert.
